Create a Conda environment

Source: R/create_env.R
create_env.Rd

Creates a Conda environment from package specs or from an environment file. With overwrite = FALSE (the default), create_env() never replaces an existing environment. It keeps the environment when it already has the requested packages. Otherwise, it aborts (see Existing environments).

Usage

create_env(
  ...,
  env_name = "condathis-env",
  method = "auto",
  verbose = c("output", "silent", "cmd", "spinner", "full"),
  channels = "conda-forge",
  additional_channels = NULL,
  channel_priority = c("strict", "flexible", "disabled"),
  platform = NULL,
  env_file = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE
)

Arguments

...

Package match specs (MatchSpec strings), unnamed: character strings or character vectors, in order. Examples: "python=3.13", "bioconda::fastqc==0.12.1". With no specs, create_env() creates an empty environment. Any other value aborts with class condathis_create_env_invalid_packages. Such values are:

  • A named argument that create_env() does not have. Names are never abbreviated: env = and pack = abort too. The error names the closest argument.

  • A value that is not a character vector.

  • NA or "".

  • A file name that ends in .yml or .yaml. Pass it as env_file.

packages = <specs> still works, and packages = NULL creates an empty environment. It is deprecated. It warns once per session (class condathis_deprecated_packages_arg) when the call comes from the console, a script or the tests of the package that makes it. Calls made inside other packages do not warn.

create_env() aborts with class condathis_create_env_positional_env_name when env_name is not given, the specs are two or more unnamed arguments, and the last of them is one string that names an existing environment. Name the argument, as in env_name = "my-env". Specs given with packages = or as one vector are never checked this way.

env_name

Character string with the environment name. It must be a plain directory name that is valid on Linux, macOS and Windows:

  • Not empty, and not . or ...

  • Not starting with -, and not ending with ..

  • Without path separators, :, #, whitespace, control characters or <>"|?*.

  • Not a Windows device name, such as NUL or COM1 (see Environment names in create_env()).

Invalid values abort with class condathis_invalid_env_name. run(), run_bin(), run_pipeline() and run_step() also accept an env_path() value. The other functions reject it with class condathis_env_path_read_only.

method

Character string naming the backend. "auto" (the default) uses the backend that owns env_name when it exists, and otherwise the first available backend in getOption("condathis.backend_priority") order (see condathis-options). Any name from list_registered_backend_names() selects that backend, and "micromamba" is built in. The name of a backend whose package condathis knows, such as "rattler" of the rattlerthis package, also selects it. condathis loads the package on first use. "native" is a deprecated alias for "micromamba" (warns once per session). The 0.1.4 default c("native", "auto") is read as "native".

If you name a backend other than the owner, functions that change the environment abort. The others warn and use the owner. The classes:

  • condathis_backend_not_installed: the package of the named backend is not installed.

  • condathis_backend_mismatch: the named backend does not own the environment, and the function changes it.

  • condathis_backend_mismatch_warning (a warning): the same, for a function that does not change the environment.

  • condathis_backend_ambiguous_env: several backends have an environment of that name, and method names none of them.

  • condathis_invalid_method: an invalid value.

verbose

Character string that controls the console output. One of:

  • "output": show the output of the command and the messages of condathis.

  • "silent": show nothing.

  • "cmd": show the command line.

  • "spinner": show only a spinner.

  • "full": show the command line, the output, and the backend's own log.

TRUE means "output" and FALSE means "silent". Every level except "silent" shows a spinner in interactive sessions. It also shows these messages and this warning when they occur (see condathis-conditions):

  • condathis_micromamba_downloading (a message): no usable micromamba was found, so it is downloaded. Queries, such as list_envs(), never download it.

  • condathis_env_lock_waiting and condathis_cache_lock_waiting (messages): the call waits for another R session.

  • condathis_install_micromamba_checksum_unavailable (a warning): the checksum of the downloaded micromamba could not be checked.

Invalid values abort with class condathis_invalid_verbose. The default is shown in Usage.

The command line shown, the cmd of a result and the messages of condathis show the password and the token of a URL as *****. micromamba does the same (https://user:*****@host/channel, https://host/t/*****/channel). The command still gets them.

channels

A non-empty character vector of channel names or URLs, in priority order. For a package from another channel, either name the channel in the spec ("bioconda::samtools") or add it here, as in channels = c("conda-forge", "bioconda"). Invalid values, such as NULL, NA or "", abort with class condathis_create_env_invalid_channels. condathis 0.1.4 also used "bioconda" by default. When channels is not given and the backend finds no package for a spec, the error says that the default changed.

additional_channels

NULL (the default) or a non-empty character vector of channel names or URLs, used after channels. Invalid values abort with these classes:

  • condathis_create_env_invalid_channels

  • condathis_invalid_additional_channels

channel_priority

Channel priority mode: "strict" (the default), "flexible" or "disabled". With "strict", when several channels have a package, the solver uses only the builds from the first of them. This keeps the solution reproducible. The mamba documentation recommends this setting. Invalid values abort with class condathis_create_env_invalid_channel_priority.

platform

NULL (the default) or the platform for the solver: a known conda platform (subdir) name in lower case, such as "linux-64", "linux-aarch64", "osx-64", "osx-arm64", "win-64", "win-arm64" or "emscripten-wasm32". Other values abort with class condathis_create_env_invalid_platform before anything runs. The message suggests a close name, such as "linux-aarch64" for "linux-arm64". When the channels have no packages for a known platform, the backend fails. Then create_env() aborts with class condathis_create_env_failed. With NULL, condathis can fall back to an emulated platform. This happens when the package specs or the env_file cannot be installed for the native platform, dependencies included, but can for the emulated one. This works with every backend that can tell whether a request solves for a platform, micromamba included. On Apple Silicon, condathis uses "osx-64" when Rosetta 2 is available. With a backend that solves for "win-arm64", condathis uses "win-64" through x64 emulation. The win-arm64 micromamba, which a native ARM64 R on Windows installs, is such a backend. install_packages() later installs packages for the platform that the environment was created for, given or emulated. For an existing environment, see Existing environments.

env_file

NULL (the default) or the path of an environment YAML file. With the micromamba backend, condathis passes it to micromamba create -f. No backend applies the variables: of a YAML file: the commands that run in the environment do not get them. Do not use both package specs and env_file: that aborts with class condathis_create_env_conflicting_args. A file that does not exist aborts with class condathis_create_env_missing_env_file.

overwrite

TRUE or FALSE (the default). With FALSE, create_env() never replaces an existing environment. create_env() keeps the environment and runs nothing when it has every requested package (see Existing environments) or when no package is requested. It returns status 0. Otherwise, and always when env_file is set, create_env() aborts with class condathis_create_env_exists. Use install_packages() to add packages to an existing environment. Use validate_env() to check one. With TRUE, create_env() creates the environment again from scratch, also when it exists or was built for another platform. When create_env() fails to create the new environment (a misspelled package, a download error), it keeps the existing one as it was. When it cannot move the existing one aside first (on Windows, while a program uses one of its files), it aborts with class condathis_create_env_failed and changes nothing. Invalid values abort with class condathis_create_env_invalid_overwrite.

Value

A condathis_result object, invisibly: a classed list with status, stdout, stderr, timeout, pid, cmd and env_name. cmd is the command line that the backend ran, or NA when the backend reports none. cmd, stdout and stderr are NA when nothing ran (an existing environment that already has the requested packages). stdout, stderr and pid are NA when the backend reports none, and pid always is with micromamba. A backend failure aborts with class condathis_create_env_failed (also condathis_backend_error), with the backend's error as the parent. micromamba runs the link scripts of packages (pre-link and post-link). A backend that does not, such as "rattler" of the rattlerthis package, makes create_env() warn. The warning names the packages, which may not work. Its classes are condathis_link_scripts_skipped and
condathis_create_env_link_scripts_skipped.

Details

With the micromamba backend, create_env() adds the new environment to ~/.conda/environments.txt, the registry that conda and mamba share. It does so only when micromamba needs your home directory, for example for channel credentials you saved there (see Details in get_install_dir()).

Existing environments

With overwrite = FALSE, create_env() compares an existing environment with the request. validate_env() makes the same comparison.

An installed package satisfies a spec when it matches the name, version, build string and channel of the spec. The name match ignores case: "PyYAML" matches pyyaml. A spec without a channel must match a package from channels or additional_channels. The channel comparison ignores credentials and platform subdirectories, and compares a local channel by its absolute path. "defaults" matches the pkgs/main and pkgs/r packages it installs. The comparison uses only these bracket constraints: version, build, build_number and channel. >=1.2.* is read as >=1.2, as micromamba does. A build string matches with * as its only wildcard.

A package from another channel does not satisfy a spec without a channel. An environment built with condathis 0.1.4, which also used "bioconda" by default, can have such packages. The error then names the channel of the package. Add that channel to channels, or name it in the spec, as in "bioconda::samtools".

Specs for virtual packages, whose names start with __, such as "__cuda=12", "__unix" or "__glibc>=2.17", are not compared. They describe the host, not the environment, and are never installed. The solver checked them when it created the environment. create_env() and install_packages() still pass them to the backend.

A spec that condathis cannot compare, or that micromamba, rattler and conda read differently, never counts as satisfied. create_env() then aborts for it with class condathis_create_env_exists. These are specs with:

  • Another bracket constraint, such as "zlib[md5=...]", or a group in parentheses at the end, such as "zlib (>=1.2,<2)" (read as bracket constraints).

  • A version with * after >, <, <= or ~= ("zlib<2.*").

  • A version with * in its middle ("zlib=1.*.3", "zlib=1.3.*.*"), in !=1.2* or in =1.2*.

  • A version with * after >=, other than a single .* at the end ("zlib>=1.2*").

  • ~= with a one-part version ("zlib~=1"), an operator with no version ("zlib>=*"), a missing operand ("zlib>=1.2,"), a build_number with == ("zlib[build_number='==0']"), or a version that micromamba rejects ("zlib>==1.2").

  • A build string with a character other than a letter, a digit, _, . and *, such as a regular expression ("zlib=1.3.1=^h4.*$") or ?.

A spec that condathis cannot read aborts with one of these classes, and also with class condathis_invalid_arg:

  • condathis_parse_match_spec_invalid_name: a spec such as "::".

  • condathis_parse_match_spec_invalid_url: the URL of a package file whose name is not <name>-<version>-<build>.

For a new environment, only the backend reads the specs. A spec it cannot read aborts with class condathis_create_env_failed.

When platform is given, the platform of the installed packages must be platform (noarch packages match any platform). A different platform aborts with class condathis_create_env_platform_mismatch, and create_env() keeps the environment. With platform = NULL, the platform is not compared.

Other R sessions

Only one R session at a time changes an environment. create_env(), install_packages() and remove_env() hold a lock on the environment name while they work, with every backend. A call for an environment that another R session is changing waits until that session is done. After two seconds, the call says so with a message of class condathis_env_lock_waiting. verbose = "silent" hides this message. Ctrl-C stops the wait. clean_cache() waits until no other R session creates an environment or installs packages. Those calls wait while it cleans. Each wait gives a message of class condathis_cache_lock_waiting. A lock lasts only as long as its session, also when the session crashes or is killed. The lock files are in the directory locks of the condathis data directory (see get_install_dir()). Where files cannot be locked, such as on some network file systems, the call goes on without the lock. When it changes something, it warns once per session with class condathis_env_lock_unavailable.

Environment names

An env_name cannot be a Windows device name, on any OS. These names are CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, CONIN$, CONOUT$, COM1 to COM9 and LPT1 to LPT9, and COM or LPT followed by a superscript one, two or three. The match ignores letter case and also applies with an extension, such as nul.txt.

See also

condathis-conditions for every condition class, and condathis-options for the options that choose the backend.

Other environments: env_exists(), env_path(), get_env_dir(), install_packages(), list_envs(), list_packages(), remove_env(), validate_env()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
condathis::with_sandbox_dir({
  # A local channel shipped with condathis, with `polyglot`: a
  # dependency-free script that runs on Linux, macOS and Windows.
  channel <- system.file(
    "extdata", "polyglot-channel",
    package = "condathis"
  )

  # Create a Conda environment from that channel, without network access
  # once micromamba is installed.
  condathis::create_env(
    "polyglot",
    env_name = "polyglot-env",
    channels = channel
  )

  # A second call keeps the environment: it already has `polyglot`.
  condathis::create_env(
    "polyglot",
    env_name = "polyglot-env",
    channels = channel
  )

  # Create an empty environment.
  condathis::create_env(env_name = "empty-env")

  # Create a Conda environment and install the CLI `fastqc` in it.
  # Explicitly using the channel `bioconda` and version `0.12.1`.
  condathis::create_env(
    "bioconda::fastqc==0.12.1",
    env_name = "fastqc-env",
    verbose = "output"
  )
})
} # }
